title: Source-spec catalog document
description: One catalog file per agent family, embedded in the binary. The catalog is the Compiled tier and therefore carries the scope ceiling: roots resolve only within the agent-owned directories named here plus their documented env-var overrides, and no config layer can add a root. The ceiling is root-granular by design -- glob subsumption is deliberately not computed -- so the airtight path floor is the compiled deny list (applied after env expansion and symlink resolution) plus require_subdir. Primitives are code; sources are data: new agent coverage within an already-compiled root family is a data-file change, a genuinely new root is a release.

spec_version.description: Catalog document version. Unknown values are a hard error at load.

family.description: Storage family this file covers. ~70 known agents collapse into ~8 families; a family is the unit of coverage work.

id.description: Stable source identity. Config merges per-source on this id, it keys the fingerprint state, and it appears in the object key as source=<id>, so renaming one re-ships its history.

enabled.description: Default enablement. `enabled: false` at any local layer is the concrete local-deny-beats-remote-allow surface and no remote layer can undo it.

gather.description: Compiled collection primitive. The registry also claims the names `acp` and `cloud_pull`, deliberately absent from this enum: they are reserved so config can never introduce them, and a spec naming one fails validation until they are implemented.

artifact_class.description: Artifact class: trajectories age out safely; context artifacts are long-lived and mutated in place. Classification metadata only: retention collapsed to a single noncurrent-version window sized to the context need, so nothing downstream consumes it, but a future decision may.

roots.description: Candidate roots, first existing wins unless the primitive unions them. Entries may name env vars ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, $CODEX_HOME) and ~. Expansion happens in the client and the deny list applies to the expanded, symlink-resolved path -- never to this template, because env vars are attacker-influenceable on a compromised machine.

require_subdir.description: Refuse a root that does not look like the store it claims to be (a claimed Claude Code root with no projects/ dir). Half of the airtight path floor.

include.description: Globs relative to the resolved root, ** per the doublestar contract. Walks never follow symlinks, pairing with O_NOFOLLOW at open time.

max_file_bytes.description: Files above this ship as metadata_only inventory records instead of content.

sniff.description: Declarative structural assertion, so a drifted format is a catalog fix rather than a release. Shape only, never semantics.

enrichers.description: Registered enrichers to run for this source. Config can only enable or disable a compiled enricher -- no layer can install transformation code. For DB-backed inputs the derived view is the only carrier of the DB-side fields, so disabling one stops that capture entirely.

emit.description: sidecar only: the record kind this source emits.

cwd_probe.description: sidecar only: a bounded probe, NOT a parser. Head-of-file budget, first match wins, no record types, no version awareness, never errors, never retries.

fields.description: Field names live in config so a renamed field is a config fix, not a release.

follow_gitdir_file.description: Worktrees: .git is a file holding a gitdir: pointer.

take.description: Scan .git/config for these keys only, ignoring insteadOf, credential helpers, everything else.

allOf.$comment: Every primitive that walks the filesystem needs a root and at least one include glob.
A sidecar source derives its records from other sources, so it takes a probe rather than globs.

kind.description: jsonl: the first non-empty line parses as JSON. json: the whole file parses. magic: the leading bytes match. text: decodes as UTF-8 and is not high-entropy. none: no assertion.

magic_hex.description: magic only: expected leading bytes, lowercase hex. Catches a store that started shipping compressed or encrypted at rest.
